topic: The Magic of Pure Fourier Series: Breaking Down Waves

sections.title: The Hook: The Musical Instrument Analogy
lecture_lines: Any periodic signal is a sum of sine waves.
Think of a guitar chord as individual notes.
We can break complex sounds into simple parts.
animations: Display a complex wave form at center. (Color: #FF00FF)
Fade in individual sine wave components below. (Color: #00FFFF)
Animate components adding up into the complex wave. (Color: #FF00FF, #00FFFF)

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Language of Orthogonality
lecture_lines: Periodic functions repeat their values regularly.
Sine and cosine waves are mathematically orthogonal.
This allows us to find individual frequency components.
animations: Display two perpendicular axes at the center. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Show a sine wave and cosine wave. (Color: #00FF00 for Sine, #FF0000 for Cosine)
Display product integral equaling zero to show orthogonality. (Color: #FFFF00)

sections.title: The Core Concept: The Fourier Series Formula
lecture_lines: The Fourier series is an infinite harmonic sum.
Coefficients act like volume knobs for frequencies.
Adding harmonics gradually sharpens the signal shape.
animations: Display Fourier series formula centered on screen. (Color: #FFFFFF)
Animate a wave sharpening as terms are added. (Color: #00FF00)

sections.title: Calculating the Components
lecture_lines: We use integrals to filter specific frequencies.
The integral measures the area of overlap.
This technique extracts individual rhythmic components.

sections.title: Real-World Application: Data Compression
lecture_lines: Fourier series are essential for modern data compression.
We keep only the most important coefficients.
Discarding the rest saves significant storage space.
animations: Show low-magnitude Fourier components being removed. (Color: #FF0000)
